themes_detail.label: For-Hire Vehicle Surge
themes_detail.summary: For-hire vehicle complaints (Uber, Lyft, etc.) spiked to 35 THIS WEEK, up 146% from the 14.2-per-week baseline over the prior 8 weeks, suggesting a sudden surge in congestion, double-parking, or traffic violations tied to ride-sharing services in Fort Greene/Brooklyn Heights.
evidence: 35 for-hire vehicle complaints THIS WEEK vs. 14.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 6.01)
146% spike in a single week suggests acute, recent shift in ride-sharing behavior or enforcement
No prior news coverage or community board mention, indicating this is an under-reported emerging issue
reporting_angles: Interview residents and business owners on specific blocks about double-parking and congestion from Uber/Lyft drivers
Investigate whether TLC enforcement has changed or if ride-sharing volume has genuinely increased this week

themes_detail.label: Street Noise Explosion
themes_detail.summary: Street and sidewalk noise complaints exploded to 73 THIS WEEK, up 236% from the 21.8-per-week baseline, the second-highest z-score spike in the district, indicating a sudden, acute noise disturbance affecting outdoor public spaces.
evidence: 73 noise complaints (street/sidewalk) THIS WEEK vs. 21.8 weekly average (z-score: 4.7)
236% spike indicates a discrete, recent event or pattern—construction, street events, or new commercial activity
Fits broader neighborhood noise concern: 1,818 residential noise complaints over 90 days (top 3 issue by volume)
reporting_angles: Canvass affected blocks to identify what triggered the spike: construction projects, street festivals, new venue openings, or nightlife hotspots
Cross-reference with DOB permits filed in last 1–2 weeks to see if construction timeline aligns

themes_detail.label: Real-Time Enforcement Surge
themes_detail.summary: Real-time enforcement complaints jumped to 6 THIS WEEK from a baseline of 0.8 per week (700% spike, z-score: 4.04), suggesting sudden, concentrated enforcement activity—possibly parking sweeps, vending crackdowns, or traffic enforcement—that residents are now reporting.
evidence: 6 real-time enforcement complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.8 weekly baseline (z-score: 4.04, 700% spike)
Very low baseline (0.8/week) makes this category inherently volatile but the sudden spike suggests new city policy or operation
Illegal parking remains the top 311 complaint category (6,434 over 90 days), so enforcement activity is likely parking-related
reporting_angles: Check NYPD and DOT press releases for new enforcement initiatives or sweeps announced this week in CD 302
Interview residents and parking enforcement officers to understand what specific enforcement activity triggered complaints

themes_detail.label: Residential Sanitation Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Residential disposal complaints spiked to 7 THIS WEEK, up 154% from a 2.8-per-week baseline (z-score: 4.39), and street-sweeping complaints hit 8 LAST WEEK (611% spike from 1.1 baseline), signaling a sanitation service breakdown or new debris/litter problem in the district.
evidence: 7 residential disposal complaints THIS WEEK vs. 2.8 weekly average (z-score: 4.39, 154% spike)
8 street-sweeping complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.1 weekly baseline (z-score: 4.07, 611% spike)
Convergence of two sanitation complaint types suggests systemic city service failure rather than isolated resident issues
reporting_angles: Interview Sanitation Department about staffing levels, collection schedules, or route changes in Fort Greene/Brooklyn Heights this week
Document specific locations with visible sanitation problems (overflowing bins, uncollected debris) to illustrate resident complaints

themes_detail.label: Building/Zoning Compliance Spike
themes_detail.summary: Building/use complaints jumped to 7 LAST WEEK from a 1.2-per-week baseline (460% spike, z-score: 5.94), coinciding with active ULURP rezonings (Columbia Heights, 395 Flatbush Avenue) and 1,148 new DOB filings in 90 days, suggesting zoning conflicts or illegal use of residential/commercial spaces.
evidence: 7 building/use complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.2 weekly baseline (z-score: 5.94, 460% spike)
Three active ULURP applications (Columbia Heights Rezoning, 395 Flatbush Avenue redevelopment) in public review/filed stage
1,148 DOB permit filings in last 90 days (826 alterations alone) indicate heavy development activity; complaints may signal resident friction over construction or zoning changes
reporting_angles: Investigate what specific building/use violations residents reported last week; cross-reference with active ULURP or DOB permits
Profile the Columbia Heights rezoning or 395 Flatbush Avenue project and interview residents about perceived impacts (noise, safety, affordability concerns)
